subject: GridPay procurement: PO line items & commit policy
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: procurement@gridpay.com
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@gridpay.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: GridPay procurement: PO line items & commit policy

Hi Jordan / GridPay procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited about the opportunity to support GridPay's customer support automation with Redwood's hosted API. Per our discussion, I'm attaching the preferred vendor form and a short summary of how we typically map usage-based, per-token pricing to PO line items for enterprise procurement.

Quick summary (proposed model):
- Pricing model: committed monthly token tiers + pay-as-you-go overage
- Example SKU mapping: Committed Tokens (50M tokens @ $0.00085/token) as one line item; Overage Tokens billed monthly as a separate line item at $0.00120/token.
- True-up: we reconcile actual usage monthly and invoice the net difference; minimum invoice equals the committed amount for the month.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices, Net-30 by default (we can discuss Net-60 per your form).

Ask from you: please confirm whether GridPay's preferred vendor form requires unit pricing per "unit" (we can express price per 1M tokens), and whether procurement needs a fixed-dollar PO only (we can provide a committed-dollar line item plus a separate overage line for tracking).

Attachments: GridPay_PreferredVendorForm.pdf (filled), Redwood_PO-Terms-v1.docx (sample mapping), example-invoice-commit-mapping.pdf (sample invoice).

If that approach is acceptable I can loop in Finance and Legal to prepare a short amendment that maps the tiers to PO line items the way procurement typically expects. Open to a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@gridpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@gridpay.com, Asha Patel <asha.patel@gridpay.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GridPay procurement: PO line items & commit policy

Marissa,

Thanks for the materials and the clear summary. A few procurement constraints on our side that will affect how we accept the PO:

1) We cannot accept a pure "per-token" unit without a capped-dollar line item on the PO. Procurement requires either (a) a fixed dollar line item that represents the committed spend, or (b) explicit unit pricing where the unit is an integer quantity (e.g., price per 1,000,000 tokens).
2) Net-60 is our standard for new vendors; your form shows Net-30. We need Net-60 in the vendor agreement or an approved exception.
3) We do not allow open-ended monthly overages without a stated cap or prior written approval. If overage billing occurs, we require an explicit overage SKU and a monthly true-up invoice that lists usage quantities so our AP team can validate.
4) We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short security addendum before legal will sign.

If you can provide a sample invoice that maps the committed line item and the overage line item (with example quantities and the price-per-1M-token unit), and an amendment that sets Net-60 and shows the overage SKU/cap language, we can move forward.

Appreciate you being flexible here — procurement is just trying to make sure our AP and budgeting processes can consume the invoice.

Best,
Jordan Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
GridPay
[jordan.lee@gridpay.com]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: GridPay procurement: PO line items & commit policy

Team — forwarding GridPay's procurement reply. They can't accept open-ended per-token billing without PO line itemization, Net-60 preferred, and they require SOC2 evidence. They explicitly asked for a sample invoice that shows committed vs overage lines and price-per-1M-token units.

Proposed options to get this over the finish line:
1) Offer a mapped PO format:
   - Line 1: "Committed Token Capacity — 50,000,000 tokens @ $0.00085 per token (equiv. $850 per 1M)" (show quantity as 50 units of 1M tokens if procurement prefers integer units)
   - Line 2: "Overage / Burst Tokens — billed monthly at $0.00120 per token (or $1,200 per 1M)"
   - Monthly true-up: invoice shows both lines with actual quantities used; if usage < committed, credit the difference; if > committed, bill overage. Minimum invoice = committed spend.
2) Offer a capped overage option: agree to a maximum overage of X% of committed tokens per month before requiring written approval.
3) For Net-60: Finance can offer Net-30 + early-pay discount or accept Net-60 if procurement signs an SLA amendment. Alternatively, offer a prepay option to satisfy their Net-60 preference without creating recognition issues.

Action items: Vivek, can Finance confirm we can emit invoices with separate SKU line items and the example invoice? Also need revenue recognition note (committed vs consumed). Neha / Legal: can you prepare a short amendment to the vendor form that sets Net-60 and defines the overage SKU/cap language? Rishi: happy to jump on a call with procurement if needed.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: GridPay procurement: PO line items & commit policy

Thanks for the context. Short answers:

- We can produce invoices with discrete line items and a unit of "1,000,000 tokens" if procurement requires integer units. We'll include quantity, unit price, and extended line totals.
- For revenue recognition, we treat commits as deferred revenue and true up monthly against usage. Minimum invoice equal to committed spend is fine; we will book the committed invoice as deferred and recognize as tokens are consumed (standard practice).
- Net-60: Net-60 will cause longer DSO; Finance would prefer Net-30 but we can accept Net-60 for strategic customers if Legal approves credit terms. Alternatively, offer a prepay discount (e.g., 1.5% discount for prepaying 3 months) to align with their process.
- Overage cap: acceptable to implement a soft cap (e.g., 25% monthly overage without additional approvals) and require written approval beyond that. This solves procurement's "no open-ended overage" concern.

Please provide exact committed quantities (e.g., 50M/month) and we will generate a sample invoice. Also confirm billing address, remit-to, and tax entity for GridPay.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-04-09T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GridPay procurement: PO line items & commit policy

Jordan / Asha,

Thanks for the clarity — we've discussed options internally and can accommodate procurement's requirements. Below is the concrete format we propose for the PO and monthly invoice reconciliation. If this maps to GridPay's AP system, please confirm and we'll send an updated vendor form + DocuSign link.

Proposed PO mapping (example for first 3 months):
- Line item A: "Committed Token Capacity (per month) — 50 x 1,000,000-token units @ $850 per 1M tokens"
  - Quantity: 50 (represents 50M tokens)
  - Unit price: $850.00 (equivalent to $0.00085 per token)
  - Extended total: $42,500.00
- Line item B: "Burst / Overage Tokens (per month) — unit: 1,000,000 tokens @ $1,200 per 1M tokens"
  - Quantity: 0 (sample PO shows zero for overage; actual billed quantity will be usage-based)
  - Unit price: $1,200.00
  - Extended total: $0.00 on PO (billed on true-up invoice if used)

Monthly invoicing / true-up:
- We will issue a monthly invoice listing both line items with actual quantities consumed. If actual usage < committed, we will issue a credit for the difference. If actual usage > committed, we will bill the overage quantity on the overage SKU. Minimum invoice reflects the committed spend.
- Soft cap: overage up to 25% of committed tokens will be billed automatically; anything above that will require written approval from GridPay prior to billing.
- Payment terms: Net-60 per your vendor form. Alternatively, GridPay can elect a prepay option (3-month prepay) for a 1.5% discount.

Attached: amended vendor form with Net-60 and overage SKU language included; example-invoice-commit-mapping.pdf shows how the invoice will look. I will send a DocuSign envelope with the amendment once you confirm the PO format.

Please confirm by EOD Tue (2026-04-13) if this mapping is acceptable or if you need alternate wording for the PO line items. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to sign off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
